slides.title: It starts with a question
slides.text: Every Fairground chart began as somebody's question. Ask a muddled question and you collect muddled answers. Ask a clean one, with a handful of choices, and the chart almost draws itself.

slides.title: One class, charted
slides.text: One Netville class answered one question: how do you get to school? The answers tallied into three bars. Bus is the tallest, and the chart can already answer questions nobody has asked yet.

visual.label: A bar graph of how a class gets to school: walk 9, bus 12, bike 4; the longest bar makes 12

focus.cue: Walk: 9 students, counted from that one class.
Bus is the tallest bar: 12 students.
Bike: only 4. Small bars still count.

slides.title: Worked example: pencil lengths
slides.text: Rough first: the pencils are all near 6 inches, so the marks should crowd there. We measured five pencils: 6, 7, 6, 8 and 6 inches. On the line plot, the 6 collects a stack of three marks.
steps: Measure every pencil the same way, from the very end
Put one mark over each length on the line

visual.label: A line plot of five pencil lengths from 5 to 8 inches: three x marks over 6, one over 7 and one over 8

focus.cue: No pencil is 5 inches long: the marks start at 6.
Three pencils measure exactly 6 inches: three x marks stack here.

slides.title: Claims the data can carry
slides.text: A chart earns its keep when someone makes a claim from it. More children in this class ride the bus than walk is a claim this chart can carry. Everyone hates walking is not: the chart never asked about liking. Claim only what you counted.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for asking and counting.

words.means: asking many people the same question and collecting their answers
the ask that starts a survey; its choices decide what can be charted
counting answers with one mark for each answer as it arrives
a statement the data can carry, and no bigger than the data

slides.title: Stretch: twenty answers
slides.text: Stretch: a question with twenty different answers cannot be charted kindly. Rewrite this one so it can: what is everyone's favorite food, exactly? Stretch work is never in the check.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at My Data and finish all 3 survey cases. Each case is your own survey: pick the question, tally the answers, chart them, and pin only a claim the chart really shows.
slides.alt: Data Detective, My Data: a class survey tallied with the steppers and built into a bar chart, a claim ready to pin.
